# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why1: Right after I typed what Fresco does better than today's way, Keel shows me the benefits it drafted from my answer so I can check them before they go to strangers.

screens.why3: These are my own two claims, the time saved and texting the crew their items, and the hard case is the trailer hours I built the company around.
screens.why4: Two distinct rows, each under nine words, no overlap and no number I didn't write; the guidance says 1 to 4.
screens.why5: 'Hours back' keeps my 90%-faster claim, but my lead point, that the notes get done during the walk and not after, has become 'action items to the crew the same day', which is the texting feature rather than the shift in when the log gets written.
screens.why7: Noun-phrase benefits, one per row, equal and non-overlapping, both carried in typed order joined with 'and', against the problem clause's hurt (the trailer day) rather than any last occasion; none is something their current way already delivers.
screens.instead: Rows: 'Notes done on the walk, not after' · 'Hours back at the end of the day' · 'Action items to the crew the same day'.

screens.why1: Right after I've said what it does better, it's the obvious next thing to ask: what my supers have to take on to start using it.
screens.why2: "Setup, extra steps or learning" and "start using it" are plain to me, and I can answer in a superintendent's own terms without a second read.
screens.why3: I know exactly what a super has to change on the walk and in the trailer, so I answer this from what I've seen them do.
screens.why4: The only option is the "I'm not sure" chip beside the box, and it fits a founder who can't name the effort.
screens.why5: The box holds my two steps as I'd say them: naming who owns each item while filming, and checking the notes before they go to the crew or Procore.
screens.why7: Both rows are steps the super takes themselves, each a base-form verb phrase of at most 9 words in one voice, with no other role's sign-off and nothing Compatibility or Purchase friction already tests; 'check and fix' reads as one review step, not two efforts.

screens.why1: Right after I said what supers have to do to start, Keel shows me the efforts it drafted from that, so the screen is clearly where it should be.
screens.why2: "Name who owns each item as they film" and "check and fix the notes before they go out" are how a super talks about punch items and logs; the only snag is that the title is repeated in the intro.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does on their own walk and in their own log, saying who's on the beam and reading over notes before they hit Procore or the crew's phones.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts: one is a habit while filming, the other is a review before sending. Neither overlaps the other or is a step for another role, and none is missing given that filming and talking is already tested under Compatibility.
screens.why5: Naming the owner is mine ("needs replacement by Alex", assignees and due dates), but "check and fix the notes" comes more from the thread's hallucination sceptics than from my pitch that Fresco "does the rest", so it has drifted a little toward their framing.
screens.why7: There are two rows, within 1 to 4, each at most 9 words, each a base-form step the super takes themselves in the third person. Neither row repeats Compatibility's filming-and-talking or Purchase friction's Procore check or security review, and each can carry its own 'Only if' condition.
screens.instead: Keep both rows, but reword the second as 'Read over the notes before they go to Procore', so it names where they go and sounds less like Fresco gets them wrong.

screens.why1: Right after I wrote and checked what supers have to do to start using it, picking the one effort most likely to stop them is the obvious next step before the stranger's question.
screens.why2: Naming who owns each item as you film and checking the notes before they go out are how a super talks about action items and the daily log, so I read both at first glance.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does with their own phone on their own walk, and either one decides whether they would actually use it.
screens.why4: The two efforts are distinct, one on the walk and one after it, both in a super's words, and neither is silly; between them they cover the real catches I hear about, the narration habit and not trusting what the AI wrote.
screens.why5: Calling out the assignee while filming is my own example ('needs replacement by Alex'), and reviewing the notes before they go out is what my product asks, so the list still means what I typed.
screens.why7: Both rows fit one measure, an effort the super takes themselves; they are base-form verb phrases in the 'they' voice, two of the 1 to 4, neither repeating Compatibility or Purchase friction; the belief 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' can be held or refuted by a Yes / Only if / Probably not / No answer, and the stranger gets I can't tell.

screens.why1: At the end of the flow, just before strangers see the study, it is obvious why I'm asked whether to collect emails from people willing to try Fresco on a real job.
screens.why2: "Offer a pilot?" with "Yes, ask them" or "No pilot" is plain to me as a founder who talks about paid pilots on one site, and the hint spells out exactly what respondents will see.
screens.why3: Whether I want a list of superintendents and contractors willing to try it for real is my own call, and I can answer it at once.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers the choice completely, the two options are distinct, and no escape is needed for a founder's own decision.
screens.why5: The line respondents see, "Would you try this for real? Leave your email.", names no product, role or price, so nothing of Fresco leaks, and my Yes is kept as I picked it.

screens.why1: Choosing who asks my questions belongs right before the link goes out to supers, after the pilot offer and before the study is sent.
screens.why2: It reads plainly on first pass; the hint packs voice, on-screen text, the 400-credit cost and the text-message link into one paragraph, but each part is clear.
screens.why3: I can judge which voice a superintendent standing in a trailer or on a loud site will take seriously and hear clearly.
screens.why4: Two voices with five-second samples is distinct and usable, but for a trade that's mostly men on loud jobsites I'd want a lower, male-sounding voice offered too, and the picked answer speaks of a 'face' where the screen only speaks of a voice.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco, the contractor buyer or the price leaks into this choice, and my choice to keep the preselected interviewer is kept.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? Options: Daphne ▶ 5 s · Saskia ▶ 5 s · a male voice ▶ 5 s; the same price whichever you pick.

screens.why1: After choosing who asks the questions, picking how the superintendents answer is the obvious next step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain choices; 'Daphne' is explained right in the option, and read-and-tap is clear to a founder sending a link to supes.
screens.why3: I know my supes are on phones in a trailer or truck at the end of the day, so I can judge which format they'd take.
screens.why4: The three options are distinct and complete: the AI voice interviewer, text, or let them pick, and the descriptions say exactly what each does.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or roles leaks into the choice, and my pick 'Read and tap' sits cleanly on one option.

screens.why1: After choosing how superintendents answer, deciding who gets a link is the obvious last step before sending, and nothing earlier asked it.
screens.why2: Plain words throughout; 'Contacts page' and 'open link' are Keel's own terms but each option explains itself in one line.
screens.why3: I know which supers I can reach: the ones from our site visits around Napa and the South Bay whom I know by name.
screens.why4: The three routes are distinct and cover how I would reach supers, but there is no escape such as 'not sure yet', and the third option tacks a Google sign-in detail onto a choice about who gets a link.
screens.why5: It is a sending screen with nothing of Fresco's wording to drift, and my pick of named people is kept.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? -- People I know by name (I send each their own link) / People I found with Keel (pick a list from Contacts) / One open link I post where supers already are (Procore community, a superintendents' group)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right under the title with 'Compatibility: 4 counted', and every card repeats '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know nothing was decided and that one counted person short is why.
screens.why_b2: The tally gives the bar plainly (4 counted against 5 needed), but '7 people answered' next to '4 counted' leaves me guessing why three of my supers dropped out, and on the same three, of every belief.
screens.why_b3: The three beliefs are recognisably mine, but the relative-advantage line is garbled ('their last day spent in the trailer ... would have given them hours back'), and my solution statement repeats itself ('notes with photos, assignees and due dates' twice, 'sends ... and gets back').
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need at least one more counted super per belief, but the page never says so, and never says whether to send the study to more superintendents or why three answers did not count.
screens.why_b5: It claims nothing beyond the people who answered: n is visible, the low count is called 'too few to call' on every card, and no belief is called held.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 7 supers answered but only 4 counted on each belief (3 were not counted because …); get at least one more counted answer before any of the three can be called, and my solution in one clean sentence: supers film and talk on the walk, and Fresco turns it into notes in Procore or ACC and texts the crew their items.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' right under it, so I know why there is no verdict and which number decides it.
screens.why_b2: The bars and the 3-for, 1-against split are plain, but 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 reads like 4 of 5 must say yes, not 'no more than 1 in 3 against', so I had to read it twice to see where my bar sits.
screens.why_b3: It is my compatibility row, but the belief drops 'on commercial jobs', and the question asks about 'your last daily log' when noise on site is a site-walk question; my occasion was moved to site walk.
screens.why_b4: It says plainly that nothing is settled and that Ray's no is the one to follow up, which is a concrete next call for me to make.
screens.why_b5: The n is visible and the low n is said ('a lean, not a call'), but the 'One more thing' quote about the log waiting till morning is filed under Compatibility though it says nothing about talking over noise, which implies a theme the answers don't show.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 could talk over the noise, 1 more answer needed. Ask Ray what stopped him on his last site walk, and make the strip read '3 for of 4, bar: no more than 1 in 3 against'.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both, so I know where I stand and why.
screens.why_b2: The chart plainly shows 3 a lot, 0 a little and 1 of 4 against, but 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 took me a second look to square with 'no more than 1 in 3', since it reads like a floor rather than the bar.
screens.why_b3: The belief line carries both my benefits, 'hours back' and 'action items to the crew the same day', but the bar line keeps only 'hours back at the end of the day', and the count line calls the question 'their last daily log' when what was asked was the last trailer day.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me that one more counted superintendent would let this be called, or that Denise's 'No difference' is the one against to watch.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (5 answered, 4 counted, Luis's guess left out), the small group is named 'a lean, not a call', and 3 a lot of 4 is never called strong.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 said a lot better and one said no difference, so one more counted superintendent decides it; your bar is no more than 1 in 3 against, about both hours back and same-day action items.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats the same tie.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly show 3 for and 1 against over 5 answered, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' reads like 'four of five must say yes'. That does not match the stated rule of 'no more than 1 in 3 against', so I had to look twice to see where my bar actually sits.
screens.why_b3: The card's title, Adoption friction, and the belief 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' are the dimension and step I picked, though the bar line 'You said name who owns each item as they film' is a clumsy, ungrammatical echo of it.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me that one more counted super would settle it, or that two of my three yeses hang on naming owners adding no walk time, which is the thing I'd design for.
screens.why_b5: It names the low n, says why Luis isn't counted, calls the result 'a lean, not a call', and doesn't claim a hold from 3 of 4.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 counted, 3 for and 1 against so far, one more answer settles it; note that 2 of your 3 yeses depend on naming owners adding no time to the walk.

screens.why_b1: Both boxes open on 'Too few to call' with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' right beside it, so I know nothing is decided and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: The Compatibility line is the one I checked ('talk into their phone over the noise on site'), but the Relative advantage line comes out garbled ('their last day spent in the trailer ... would have given them hours back'); I recognise it, but it is not how I'd say it.
screens.why_b4: Nothing on the screen says what this means for Fresco or what to do next, not even 'get one more super to answer' or 'the log may not be the pain for supes who finish on site'.
screens.why_b5: The counts stay visible (1 against, 1 asked, 4 of 5 needed), and nothing claims more than one person per box said.
screens.why_b6: Both quotes tell me something I didn't type: for Ray the log loses to a slipping schedule and waits till morning, and Denise finishes hers on the tablet before the gate, so schedule and subs eat her day, not the log.
screens.instead: Too few to call (4 of 5): one more answer decides it; meanwhile the one 'against' on each line points the same way: schedule and subs crowd out the log, so the log may not be the pain for supes who already finish on site.

screens.why1: As the first screen, it sensibly checks whether I'm on the platforms the study is about before asking about my daily logs.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the two names every super at a GC knows, and 'jobs you're running' is how I'd say it myself.
screens.why3: I know exactly what software my current jobs are on, no guessing.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly, since 'any of the jobs' handles the case where one job is on Procore and another isn't, and a gate needs no escape.
screens.why5: It asks only about the platforms the founder named and says nothing about what they're building or selling.
screens.why6: It's short and said in one breath, and ACC is said as letters on site anyway; 'I'll read 2 options' for a yes or no is a touch stiff but easy to answer.

screens.why1: Right after confirming my jobs run on Procore, asking whether I did the log work in the trailer this week is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: I get it on one read, but 'upload typed logs' is not how I'd say it: I upload photos, and I type the daily log into Procore, I don't upload a typed log.
screens.why3: Whether I sat in the trailer this week getting photos and the log into Procore is something I know exactly.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, and the chips beside it belong to the story box, not the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but 'upload photos and typed logs' drifts a little from typing up the daily log after the walks into two chores bundled together.
screens.why6: It is one short question with 'Yes or no' and I could answer it on one hearing, though 'photos and typed logs' runs together a bit.
screens.why7: Yes/No in order with no escape is right, and a super who did the log on the walk can truly say No, but the clause packs two acts (photos and logs), one of the card's named pitfalls.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log in the trailer after your walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: Part 1 just asked me about uploading photos and logs in the trailer, so showing the idea now makes sense.
screens.why2: Site walk, photos, assignees, Procore, ACC and action items are all words I use every day; 'AI scribe' is new but I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I walk the job every day with my phone, so I can picture shooting clips and talking over them.
screens.why4: A card to read, no options.
screens.why5: My pain is the hours in the trailer after the walks getting it into the daily log, but the card never says daily log and the belief says it serves me 'during the site walk', which drifts off the after-the-walk part.
screens.why6: Five short sentences that sound fine read out, and Procore and ACC say fine to someone like me.
screens.instead: Keep the first two lines, end with: 'The people building it believe it would save you the time of putting the day's photos and notes into the daily log after your walks.'

screens.why1: Right after the idea card, it makes sense to ask whether I could even talk into my phone out on site, because the whole idea depends on that.
screens.why2: The words are plain, but 'your last daily log' made me read it twice: I write the log in the trailer, and the talking would happen on the walk.
screens.why3: I know how loud my last walk was near the saws and the lifts, but tying it to the log instead of the walk makes me work out which moment you mean.
screens.why4: Easily, most of the time, sometimes and no cover how it goes on a loud deck, and 'I can't tell' fits as the way out.
screens.why5: Only the idea card names Fresco, and it does so on purpose; the question itself is just about talking over site noise, in words I'd use.
screens.why6: It's short, one question, and four short options I can hold, with the escape said last.
screens.why7: This is an ability on the one could-you measure, with the four ability rungs in order and 'I can't tell' apart; it is true on some sites and false on others, so it can go either way.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have talked into your phone over the noise on site? Yes, easily; yes, most of the time; only sometimes; or no. Or say you can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the phone-on-site question, it makes sense to ask whether this thing would have beaten my long trailer nights.
screens.why2: I know the day it means, but "done that better" is loose: I'd have to work out whether it means the uploading, the log itself, or getting out of the trailer sooner.
screens.why3: I sat in the trailer this week dumping photos into Procore and typing the log, so I can answer from that day.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference, worse, plus I can't tell, covers every real answer with no overlap.
screens.why5: Apart from the idea card shown on purpose, nothing of the founder's plan slips in, and the trailer-hours day is in words I'd use.
screens.why6: The stem runs well past twenty words, and "Fresco, an AI scribe" comes again right after the card, so it's a lot to hold before the four short options.
screens.why7: There are four fixed rungs, two for and two against, in the card's order with I can't tell apart, and the hard case is the hurt day, not just any day.
screens.instead: Think of your last day stuck in the trailer for hours uploading photos and typing the log. Would Fresco have made that day better, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after asking whether Fresco would do my logs better, it's natural to ask what extra I'd have to do on the walk to make it work.
screens.why2: Saying who owns an item is how we talk on a walk, meaning which sub or which of my guys has it, so I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day and already assign items to subs in my head or my notes, so I know whether I'd call them out while filming.
screens.why4: Yes, only if it adds no walk time, probably not, and no are distinct; the condition is the real catch for me; and I can't tell fits.
screens.why5: It names a step of using the idea that was shown on purpose, in words a super would use, with nothing about the founder's plans leaking through.
screens.why6: One short question and four short options said as a list, with the escape at the end, so it's easy to hold by ear.
screens.why7: The effort is my own new habit of use, the four answers sit on one measure (two for, two against), the condition is specific to this step, and I can't tell is the one escape set apart.
